personality.description: This person is imaginative and intellectually curious, often drawn to unusual ideas, new possibilities, and creative ways of doing things. In daily habits, they tend to work flexibly and spontaneously rather than by strict plans, which can make them inconsistent with organization and follow-through, though they usually adapt easily when circumstances change. When faced with moral dilemmas, they first try to understand everyone’s perspective, lean toward compassionate and cooperative solutions, and avoid choices that would create unnecessary conflict. In group discussions, they speak quietly and thoughtfully, prefer small settings, and usually listen more than they talk, but when they do contribute their remarks are calm, considerate, and aimed at keeping the atmosphere harmonious.
traits: has assertively moved up the ranks into positions of leadership
prioritizes having control and authority over others
makes quick and definitive decisions, and once a decision is made it is usually final
has their own views of how tasks should be accomplished
uses reward and punishment to get people to follow their ideas
